name: pSEOlint
tagline: A linter for programmatically generated pages: flags thin, duplicate, and unindexable templated content before it ships.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a crawler plus a rule engine, which is one of the most one-shottable shapes in software. Pull the sitemap, fetch pages, parse the head and body, then run deterministic checks: duplicate titles, near-identical bodies across templates, missing or self-conflicting canonicals, noindex left in by accident, thin word counts, orphan pages with no internal links in. None of that needs a vendor, an API key, or a dataset you do not have. What you cannot clone is the opinion baked into someone else's rule set, the part where a human decided which of forty possible warnings actually correlate with pages getting dropped from the index. Build the linter, then spend your time arguing with your own thresholds.
coreLoopDIY: Crawls your sitemap or a URL list, parses each page, and emits a ranked report of templated-SEO smells with per-rule severity and exit codes for CI.
requirements: A sitemap.xml or a list of URLs, either live or from a local build output
Patience for tuning thresholds so the report is not 4,000 warnings long
whatYouLose: A rule set someone has already tuned against real indexing outcomes, so your first run will be mostly noise
Historical tracking: seeing that duplicate-title count creep up over three deploys instead of just today
Any hosted dashboard or shareable report for people who will never run a CLI
Maintenance as search engines change what they punish, your rules freeze on the day you write them
Nice-to-haves like rendered-DOM crawling for JS-heavy pages, which is a headless browser project of its own
moatNotes: The crawl is commodity. The calibration, which warnings are worth shipping and which are superstition, is the actual product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a linter is only useful if you trust its defaults. Anyone can generate a list of every HTML imperfection on 20,000 generated pages; the value is a short list that says these nine things are why half your directory is not indexed. Teams running programmatic SEO at scale are also usually in a hurry, and a tool that plugs into CI with sane severities on day one beats a homegrown script that needs a week of threshold arguments. If you only have a few hundred pages and one opinionated person, the homegrown script wins.
notes: The crawler is a Tuesday; the rule set is the product. Write the crawler, then steal the opinions from your own logs.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called pseo-lint that audits programmatically generated pages for SEO problems.

Stack, no substitutions: TypeScript on Node 20, run via tsx, dependencies limited to commander (CLI), undici (fetch), cheerio (HTML parsing), fast-xml-parser (sitemaps), p-limit (concurrency), picocolors (output). No framework, no database, no accounts, no telemetry.

Inputs, support both:
1. pseo-lint crawl --sitemap https://example.com/sitemap.xml --limit 500
2. pseo-lint crawl --urls urls.txt
Also support --dir ./dist to lint static HTML files on disk without any network calls.

Respect robots.txt, default concurrency 4, default delay 200ms, configurable user agent.

Implement these rules, each with an id, severity, and a one-line human explanation:
- missing or empty title, title over 60 chars, duplicate title across pages
- missing meta description, duplicate meta description
- missing canonical, canonical pointing to a different page than the one fetched, conflicting canonicals
- noindex or nofollow in meta robots or X-Robots-Tag header
- word count below a configurable threshold (default 150) in the main content area
- template similarity: compute a shingled hash of the body text, cluster pages above a configurable Jaccard threshold (default 0.9), report cluster sizes
- heading problems: zero h1, multiple h1, h1 identical to title across large clusters
- internal links: pages with fewer than 2 internal inbound links found during the crawl (orphan risk), pages with zero outbound internal links
- broken internal links (HEAD request, 4xx or 5xx)
- non-200 status or redirect chain longer than 1 hop for a sitemap URL

Output: a colored terminal summary grouped by rule and sorted by count, plus --json report.json and --html report.html (single self-contained file, no CDN assets). Exit code 1 if any error-severity rule fires, 0 otherwise, so it drops into CI.

Config via pseolint.config.json: thresholds, rule severities, rule disabling, URL ignore globs. Ship a sensible default config and a README with three example invocations.

Explicitly out of scope: keyword volume data, rank tracking, Search Console or any OAuth integration, JS rendering via headless browser, hosted dashboards, historical trend storage. Put nothing in .env unless a custom auth header is needed for staging sites; if so, read PSEOLINT_AUTH_HEADER from .env via node --env-file.

Write unit tests with node:test for the rule functions using HTML fixtures, no network in tests.
